docs.title: What is an API?
docs.text: Application Programming Interface (API) is a set of rules and protocols that allows different software applications to communicate with each other.

docs.title: REST (Representational State Transfer)
docs.text:
• Most popular for web APIs
  • Resource-based
  • Uses HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH
  • Stateless communication
  • JSON/XML responses

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
• Query language for APIs
  • Request only needed data
  • Strong typing
  • Single endpoint

docs.title: SOAP (Simple Object Access Protocol)
docs.text:
• XML-based
  • More complex
  • Enterprise systems
  • WSDL contracts

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text:
• High-performance
  • Protocol Buffers
  • Bi-directional streaming

docs.title: HTTP Methods
docs.text:
Text Only
GET     → Retrieve data (idempotent)
POST    → Create new data
PUT     → Replace entire resource
PATCH   → Partial update
DELETE  → Remove data
HEAD    → Like GET but no response body
OPTIONS → Describe communication options

docs.title: Success (2xx)
docs.text:
• 200 OK: Request successful
  • 201 Created: Resource created
  • 204 No Content: Success, no body

docs.title: Client Error (4xx)
docs.text:
• 400 Bad Request: Invalid input
  • 401 Unauthorized: Authentication required
  • 403 Forbidden: Access denied
  • 404 Not Found: Resource not found
  • 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limited

docs.title: Server Error (5xx)
docs.text:
• 500 Internal Server Error: Server error
  • 503 Service Unavailable: Temporarily down

docs.title: REST Constraints
docs.text: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style based on 6 constraints:

docs.title: 1. Client-Server
docs.text:
• Separation of concerns
  • Client: UI and user experience
  • Server: Data storage and business logic
  • Allows independent evolution

docs.title: 2. Stateless
docs.text:
Text Only
Each request contains all information needed
No session data stored on server
Each request is independent
↓
Easy scalability
Easy caching

docs.title: 3. Uniform Interface
docs.text:
Text Only
Resources identified in requests (URIs)
Resources manipulation via representations
Self-descriptive messages
Hypermedia As The Engine Of Application State (HATEOAS)

docs.title: 4. Cacheable
docs.text:
Text Only
Responses marked as cacheable or non-cacheable
HTTP caching headers:
  - Cache-Control
  - ETag
  - Last-Modified

docs.title: 5. Layered System
docs.text:
Text Only
Architecture divided into layers
Each layer provides service to the layer above
Examples: Load balancer, proxy, cache, API gateway

docs.title: 6. Code on Demand (Optional)
docs.text:
Text Only
Server can extend client functionality
Example: JavaScript from server

docs.title: Idempotent Operations
docs.text:
Text Only
Multiple identical requests produce same result

GET    /users/1         → Idempotent (returns same user)
PUT    /users/1         → Idempotent (replaces same user)
DELETE /users/1         → Idempotent (deletes same user)

docs.title: Non-Idempotent Operations
docs.text:
Text Only
POST /users             → NOT idempotent (creates new user each time)
PATCH /users/1/balance → NOT idempotent (different amounts added)

Richardson Maturity Model

Text Only
Level 0: Swamp of POX

Level 1: Resources

  Still mostly POST

Level 2: HTTP Verbs & Status Codes
  GET, POST, PUT, DELETE
  200, 404, 500 status codes
  Mostly RESTful

Level 3: HATEOAS
  Hypermedia links in responses
  Self-describing API
  True REST

docs.title: Python - httpx
docs.text:
Modern async support

Python
import httpx
import asyncio

# Sync
with httpx.Client() as client:
    response = client.get("https://api.example.com/users")

# Async
async def fetch_users():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        response = await client.get("https://api.example.com/users")
        return response.json()

asyncio.run(fetch_users())

docs.title: pytest-httpserver
docs.text:
Mock HTTP server for testing

Python
import pytest
from pytest_httpserver import HTTPServer

def test_api_with_mock(httpserver: HTTPServer):
    httpserver.expect_request("/users").respond_with_json(
        {"status": "success", "data": []}
    )

    # Your code that calls the mock server
    response = requests.get(httpserver.url_for("/users"))
    assert response.json()["status"] == "success"

import requests

def test_create_user():

docs.title: What is AWS?
docs.text: Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a comprehensive cloud computing platform that offers a wide range of services to help businesses, organizations, and individuals build, deploy, and manage applications and infrastructure on the internet.

docs.title: Why Cloud Computing?
docs.text:
• Cost Efficiency: Pay only for what you use
  • Scalability: Scale up or down as needed
  • Reliability: Multiple redundancy and backup options
  • Security: Industry-leading security features
  • Performance: Global infrastructure for low latency

docs.title: AWS Global Infrastructure
docs.text:
Text Only
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│      AWS Global Infrastructure      │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Regions (Geographic Locations)     │
│    └─ Availability Zones (AZs)     │
│        └─ Data Centers             │
│            └─ Edge Locations       │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Regions
docs.text:
• Geographic areas with multiple Availability Zones
  • Isolated from other regions
  • Compliance and data sovereignty benefits

docs.title: Availability Zones (AZs)
docs.text:
• Physically separate data centers within a region
  • Connected by high-speed, low-latency networking
  • Enable high availability and disaster recovery

docs.title: Compute
docs.text:
• EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud): Virtual machines
  • Lambda: Serverless computing
  • ECS: Container orchestration
  • Elastic Beanstalk: Platform as a Service

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
• S3 (Simple Storage Service): Object storage
  • EBS (Elastic Block Store): Block storage for EC2
  • EFS (Elastic File System): Managed NFS
  • Glacier: Long-term archive storage

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
• RDS (Relational Database Service): Managed relational databases
  • DynamoDB: NoSQL database
  • Elasticache: In-memory caching
  • Redshift: Data warehouse

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
• VPC (Virtual Private Cloud): Isolated network
  • Route 53: DNS service
  • CloudFront: CDN service
  • ELB (Elastic Load Balancer): Load balancing

docs.title: Management & Monitoring
docs.text:
• CloudWatch: Monitoring and logging
  • CloudTrail: API audit logging
  • CloudFormation: Infrastructure as Code
  • Systems Manager: Resource management

docs.title: AWS Pricing Model
docs.text:
Text Only
Total Cost = Compute + Storage + Data Transfer + Additional Services

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
• On-Demand: Pay-as-you-go pricing
  • Reserved Instances: Commit for 1-3 years, get discounts
  • Spot Instances: Bid on unused capacity, up to 90% discount
  • Savings Plans: Flexible pricing for compute usage

docs.title: Getting Started with AWS
docs.text:
1. Create AWS Account: Go to aws.amazon.com
  2. Set up IAM Users: Don't use root account for daily tasks
  3. Enable MFA: Multi-Factor Authentication for security
  4. Create VPC: Isolate your resources
  5. Launch First Instance: Start with EC2

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
AWS Best Practices

  • Use IAM roles instead of access keys
  • Enable CloudTrail for audit logging
  • Use VPCs for network isolation
  • Apply security groups and NACLs
  • Enable versioning on S3 buckets
  • Use CloudWatch for monitoring
  • Implement auto-scaling
  • Use CloudFormation for IaC

docs.text:

  4. Database: RDS, DynamoDB, backup strategies

docs.title: What is EC2?
docs.text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) is a web service that provides resizable compute capacity. It's designed to make web-scale cloud computing easier for developers.

docs.title: General Purpose (t3, t3a, m5)
docs.text:
• Balance of compute, memory, and networking
  • Web applications and small databases
  • Best for: Web servers, development environments

docs.title: Compute Optimized (c5, c6i)
docs.text:
• High performance processors

class LoginPage:

docs.text:
Answer:

Synchronization Problem:

Text Only
Application doesn't load in expected time
→ Flaky tests
→ Unreliable results

Solutions:

  1. Implicit Wait (Global)

    Python
    driver.implicitly_wait(10)  # Wait 10s for any element

  2. Explicit Wait (Recommended)

    Python
    from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC

element = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.presence_of_element_located(("id", "myElement"))
)

  3. Wait for Conditions

    Python
    # Wait for network idle
page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")

# Wait for element
page.wait_for_selector("button.submit", timeout=5000)

# Wait for function
page.wait_for_function("() => document.querySelectorAll('li').length > 5")

  4. Avoid Hard Waits

    Python
    # ❌ Bad
import time
time.sleep(5)

# ✅ Good
page.wait_for_selector("button", timeout=5000)

def transfer_money(from_account, to_account, amount):
    with db.transaction():
        # Lock account for duration of transfer

docs.title: Description

SQL Injection

Python
# ❌ VULNERABLE

# Input: ' OR '1'='1  → Returns all users!

# ✅ SECURE: Use parameterized queries

Python
# ❌ VULNERABLE

# Input: "; rm -rf /  → Dangerous!

# ✅ SECURE
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["ls", "-la", user_directory], check=True)

return f"<h1>Welcome {user_input}</h1>"

docs.title: Secure API Testing
docs.text:
Python
import requests
from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth

def test_api_security():
    # Test HTTPS enforcement
    response = requests.get("http://api.example.com/users", allow_redirects=False)
    assert response.status_code == 301  # Should redirect to HTTPS

    # Test authentication required
    response = requests.get("https://api.example.com/admin")
    assert response.status_code == 401

    # Test authorization
    headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer user_token"}
    response = requests.delete("https://api.example.com/users/admin_user", headers=headers)
    assert response.status_code == 403  # Forbidden

    # Test input validation
    payload = {"name": "'; DROP TABLE users; --"}
    response = requests.post("https://api.example.com/users", json=payload)
    assert response.status_code == 400
